name: Darai
confidence_why: No first-hand description of Darai stress exists, since Dhakal's 2011 grammar and Kotapish & Kotapish's 1975 glossary say nothing about it, and the only two statements are opposed survey codings: Easterday 2019 lists fixed word stress without naming the syllable, while the LAPSyD entry (Maddieson et al. 2022) lists no stress on the strength of listening to recordings, so the placement, and even whether Darai has word stress, remains undetermined.

catalog_quote: Easterday 2019: 384: "Suprasegmentals / Tone: No / Word stress: Yes / Stress placement: Fixed / Phonetic processes conditioned by stress: Vowel reduction / Differences in phonological properties of stressed and unstressed syllables: Not described / Phonetic correlates of stress: Not described" ... "Vowel reduction processes / dry-R1: High back vowel /u/ may be deleted preceding a sequence of /wa/ and another consonant (Kotapish & Kotapish 1973: 49)." Easterday 2019: 303: "Both languages have word stress and vowel reduction. While both languages have vowel deletion, such processes are conditioned by stress only in Albanian." LAPSyD, Darai code 638: "Stresscat: ... None ... Stress: No discussion of stress in Kotapish & Kotapish (1973, 1975). Listening to recordings suggests very equal stress on most syllables apart from in phrase-final position."

The bracketed LAPSyD contrast is also verbatim in the held : the sel…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Easterday's survey codes Darai as having word stress with fixed (non-lexical, non-weight-sensitive) placement, but does not say on which syllable; LAPSyD, working from the same SIL phonemic summary plus recordings, codes no word stress and reports roughly even prominence except phrase-finally. No primary description seen states a stress position.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any source seen.
new_statements.domain_note: Easterday's coding is word-level typological coding without page citation; LAPSyD's remark is an auditory impression from recordings and points to phrase-final prominence (phrase-level) rather than word stress. The accessible primary grammar (Dhakal 2011 PhD, Chitwan dialect) treats only intonation (falling for statements/commands/wh-questions, rising for yes-no questions) and is silent on word stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Two dialects are described under dara1250: Kotapish & Kotapish 1973/1975 and Paudyal 2003 describe Tanahun (Pipaltar) Darai; Dhakal 2011/2012 describes Chitwan (Pidrahani) Darai. Dhakal notes the dialects differ in 'accent' (sociolinguistic sense) and verb agreement. Easterday's and LAPSyD's codings both rest mainly on the Tanahun-based SIL phonemic summary.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Darai has an empty rule; the existing statement (Easterday 2019, Appendix B p. 384) carries the identical coding, so this 2017 dissertation is the same second-hand coding in its earlier form and adds nothing on placement. It refines the empty catalog rule only to the extent 'word stress present, non-tonal, fixed placement (position not stated)'; it does not supply a syllable position. It is compatible with, but weaker than, the 2019 book; neither gives a position. Note the primary sources already held by the project (Dhakal 2011 PhD ch. 3; Kotapish & Kotapish 1975 glossary) are silent on stress, and LAPSyD (code 638) codes Stresscat = None with the remark that recordi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Darai is coded as a non-tonal language with word stress whose placement is 'Fixed', which in the dissertation's own key means stress falls at a predictable position relative to a word edge. The dissertation never says which syllable (initial, penultimate, final..) carries it, gives no page citation for the classification, and marks phonological differences and phonetic correlates of stress as 'Not described'. So the only content is: stress exists, is not tonal, and is edge-fixed, position unknown.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. Internal inconsistency: the appendix line 'Phonetic processes conditioned by stress: Vowel Reduction' conflicts with Table 8.6 (p. 489), which gives the Darai vowel-reduction environment as 'Consonant', and with the text on p. 490, which says vowel deletion is 'conditioned by stress only in Albanian'; the single Darai reduction rule dry-R1 (p. 574) is /u/-deletion before /wa/+C, conditioned by consonants, not stress. The entry also cites 'Kotapish & Kotapish (1978)' although the reference list has only the 1973 Darai phonemic summary.
new_statements.identity_note: Easterday 2017 does not name a dialect; its sources cover both the Chitwan variety (Dhakal 2012, Pidrahani) and the Tanahun variety (Kotapish & Kotapish, Pipaltar). The Darai entry is the language as a whole.

readall_conflicts: The only work in scope (Easterday 2017) codes Darai as 'Word stress: Yes / Stress placement: Fixed' without naming the syllable, without a page citation to any Darai source, and with an internal contradiction about whether vowel reduction is stress-conditioned (appendix says yes; Table 8.6 and p. 490 say no, 'conditioned by stress only in Albanian'). Its sources of record - Dhakal 2012 (the 2011 TU dissertation held by the project has no stress statement in its phonology chapter), Kotapish & Kotapish 1973 (not obtainable; LAPSyD reports 'No discussion of stress in Kotapish & Kotapish (1973, 1975)'), Paudyal 2003 (not obtainable) and a personal communication from N. P. Paudyal - do not visibly support a fixed-stress coding, and the personal communication is most likely where the classification came from. So the sources disagree: Easterday 2017/2019 'fixed (position unstated)' vs LAPSyD 'no stress category, phrase-final prominence'. No source opened gives a syllable position.
